body:
Tested this with some custom plugin and overall it works. You can create and edit a global plugin and it works correctly. Although as mentioned in my previous comment, the synchronization between running editor instances is a bit flawed.

I noticed there are lots of magic numbers related to plugin's scope in the code. They should all be replaced with a proper enum.

there a few usability issues:
- classes from an editor addon shouldn't appear by default in the Create node. It shoudl either be in the Editor Filter or in a new Custom Editor Filter
- Referencing a class or a path in "editor://" from "res://" or the reverse should result in a warning 
- One way I could see a use for a plugin to be both editor-wide and project-wide would be to have one that is actually project-wide but that you want enabled in all project. 
If that is the intended usecas I would prefer a separate interface in a sub tab similar to GDEXTENSION from project settings to especially deal with those. 
It should have a list of all project-wide plugins in "editor://" with the same functionality as the other for editing plus a check on wether the plugin should be auto-installed when creating a project and a button to install the plugin in the current project.
- I'm not a fan of the project-wide terminology especially the "-wide" make it seems there is a way to have something on a narrower scope.

Overall core and editor code looks good, there seems to be few places in Android code and file dialog with missing handling for new file system mode.

Editor plugins seems to be working as expected.

Needs testing with Android editor.
Needs rebase.

Some minor UI issues:
- `editor://` paths added to favorites in FS tab are still shown if you disable editor FS display, clicking such item do nothing - probably should be either hidden or auto enable editor FS display when clicked.
- enabling/disabling editor FS display rest folders to collapsed state, ideally it should save and restore previous state.

Functionality-wise it's fine now.

Needs more reviews, it's a big change.

Tested locally on the plugins demo (to make sure project-wide plugins still work correctly), it works as expected. Code looks good to me. Some feedback: - I'm a tad confused by the UX between the "project + editor" scope available in the Project Settings and the one in the Editor Settings. Both options seem like they achieve the same thing at first, but they create the plugin in different locations on the filesystem. - There could be tooltips to explain what each scope does exactly (with different texts in the project settings and editor settings). - In the list of project plugins, should we have a distinction between project-wide only plugins and project + editor plugins? The same applies to editor-wide only plugins and project + editor plugins in the Editor Settings' plugins tab. - The plugin's scope is currently stored as the integer value of the enum in `plugin.cfg`: ```ini scope=2 ``` For readability purposes, we may want to store a string representing the enum value instead, similar to the stretch mode/aspect project settings. The rest of the file is very human-readable currently, so it's odd to have it stand out like that. ```ini [plugin] name="Editor and Project" description="Example plugin that runs both in the editor and project." author="Calinou" version="0.1.0" scope=2 script="editor_and_project.gd" ```

**Current build:**
**Feedback:** Let's not add a new top-level button to the header, it's not hot enough to need to always be on screen and there will be other new features in the future competing for the fs dock header space. For now It will be better to combine it with the sorting menu:
Let's also not add gray color under global fs, there doesn't seem to be any good reason to do that and global fs will usually be hidden. In editor settings it would help to have a button to open the plugins folder in os to make it easier for users to manage them and give extra visibility into where they are actually located on disk. Something like this:
UX looks ok otherwise

Retested it on macOS and Android, seems to be working as expected. Code looks good. Few minor things: - If you use old plugin, without set scope, it will show warning icon, but there's no way to check the warning text on Android, I would duplicate it in the edit dialog description. - Should there be a `delete/uninstall` button in the editor settings tab? I would expect removing plugins be possible without manual file manipulations.
